description.value: A pilot feasibility study examining the effects of Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement on frontostriatal reward processes among cigarette smokers.

spans.text: The primary goal of this pilot feasibility study was to examine the effects of Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement (MORE), a behavioral treatment grounded in dual-process models derived from cognitive science, on frontostriatal reward processes among cigarette smokers.

value: MORE may restructure reward processes by attenuating drug cue reactivity in the ventral striatum and potentiating prefrontal and striatal responses during positive emotion regulation.
MORE would strengthen resting-state functional connectivity in frontostriatal circuitry involved in appraising the value of reward-predicting stimuli.

description.value: Structural images were bias-corrected, segmented with partial-volume estimation, denoised, warped to MNI space using the DARTEL IXI-550 template, and resampled to 1.5-mm voxels. Functional images underwent slice-time correction, realignment, motion-outlier detection and interpolation-based correction, optional despiking, coregistration to the structural image, MNI warping and resampling, and 10-mm FWHM smoothing. Resting-state data were denoised with white-matter, CSF, and motion regressors, band-pass filtered from 0.008 to 0.09 Hz, and analyzed with conn14 for SPM12.

spans.text: Dual-systems models posit that addiction is subserved by dysregulated interactions between the ventral striatum (VS), a region that codes for the predictive value of a rewarding stimulus (e.g., food, sex, and cigarette) [ 4 ], and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) that executes attentional control [ 5 ], that is, frontostriatal circuitry.

Positive Emotion Regulation Task.
The study utilizes an event-related ER paradigm that was comprised of a total of 100 trials, each presented for 14 sec, separated by a mean jittered fixation of 4 sec in duration (range 1–7 sec).

For the CR and ER tasks, participant's preprocessed fMRI data from each session were entered into a first-level analysis using the General Linear Model [ 37 ] to examine BOLD response during (CR) smoking cue versus neutral blocks and (ER) each of the 3 trial types: view positive, reappraise positive, anda neutral view.

description.value: Participants viewed a positive emotional picture while following the look instruction, without being instructed to reappraise it, and then rated their current feeling.

description.value: Participants viewed a positive emotional picture while following the reappraise instruction: they imagined experiencing the depicted positive event, focused on enjoyable aspects of the image, and focused on their positive emotional response, then rated their current feeling.

description.value: Participants viewed a neutral picture with the look instruction and then rated their current feeling.

spans.text: Finally, an 8-point rating scale was presented for 6 sec that prompted participants to indicate from 1 (most negative) to 8 (most positive) their current feeling in response to the prior picture.

description.value: Event-related positive emotion regulation paradigm with 100 trials. Each trial lasted 14 seconds and was followed by a mean 4-second jittered fixation. Participants first saw a look or reappraise instruction overlaid on a positive or neutral picture, then viewed the picture alone while implementing the instruction, and finally rated their current feeling on an 8-point scale. The task was presented in four six-minute runs.

instructions.value: For look trials, participants viewed the picture. For reappraise trials, they were instructed to imagine the positive event occurring in the picture, focus on its enjoyable aspects, and focus on their own positive emotional response. They then rated their current feeling from 1, most negative, to 8, most positive.

stimuli.value: Positive and neutral images from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS); positive images had valence/arousal values of 7.0/5.3, while neutral images had valence 4–6 and arousal below 3. Images were presented only once per participant.

value: self-reported affective rating after each trial
